hunks.baseline: Everything that lives is born with a destiny of struggle.
hunks.sol: Everything alive is born into a struggle.

hunks.baseline: Humans, monsters, animals living in the wild or behind fences, even green plants—all the same.
hunks.sol: Humans, monsters, animals in the wild or behind fences, even green plants—all of them.

hunks.baseline: Even when survival itself wasn’t the reason to struggle, you had to fight and take what you wanted.
hunks.sol: Even when survival wasn’t at stake, you had to fight to get what you wanted.

hunks.baseline: And under this absolute law, I was no exception.
hunks.sol: I was no exception to that rule.

hunks.baseline: The least force. The least speed.
hunks.sol: Minimum force. Minimum speed.

hunks.baseline: But that was enough. I twisted away, leaving behind the fanatic collapsing with his brains splattered everywhere.
hunks.sol: That was enough. I twisted aside, leaving behind a fanatic who collapsed with his brains spilling out.

hunks.baseline: Between the pitch-black robe and turban that covered him completely, I saw his eyes widen. The White Flame’s spearhead was reflected in them.
hunks.sol: Between the pitch-black robe and turban covering him, I saw his eyes widen. White Flame’s spearhead was reflected in them.

hunks.baseline: A head flew up. More enemies and their auras surged through the spraying blood.
hunks.sol: His head flew up. More enemies and their auras surged through the spraying blood.

hunks.baseline: Watching blades rush at me from every direction, I tightened my grip on the spear shaft, slick with blood.
hunks.sol: As blades came at me from every direction, I tightened my grip on the blood-slick spear shaft.

hunks.baseline: I breathed out. The world slowed. My relaxed muscles loosened, and the flames coiling around my spearhead flickered.
hunks.sol: I breathed out. The world slowed. My muscles loosened, and the flames coiling around my spearhead flickered.

hunks.baseline: Like the tail of something caught in the wind.
hunks.sol: Like a tail fluttering in the wind.

hunks.baseline: Flames surged. The enemies’ auras flashing from every direction drove away the darkness racing toward the dim dawn.
hunks.sol: Flames surged. The enemies’ auras flashed from every direction, driving back the darkness as dawn approached.

hunks.baseline: And I smoothly spun my whole body.
hunks.sol: I turned, my whole body moving in one smooth motion.

hunks.baseline: Blue-white flames streaked across the space. They were faster than any aura bearing down on me, sharper than anything anyone could stop.
hunks.sol: Blue-white flames swept across the space between us. They were faster than any aura bearing down on me, their edge too sharp for anyone to stop.

hunks.baseline: With a cool, clean cut, a sword in someone’s hand tilted to one side.
hunks.sol: With a clean, cold sound, a sword tilted in its wielder’s hand.

hunks.baseline: But no words or actions could stop death from bearing down without mercy.
hunks.sol: But nothing they said or did could stop death from coming for them.

hunks.baseline: Flames raced along the faint lines, devouring the enemies’ lives.
hunks.sol: Flames raced along the faint lines, devouring their lives.

hunks.baseline: Dense mists of blood spewed in every direction, blanketing the battlefield’s thick, low-lying steam.
hunks.sol: Thick sprays of blood mist blanketed the steam hanging low over the battlefield.

hunks.baseline: A rain of blood fell from overhead.
hunks.sol: Blood rained down on my head.

hunks.baseline: At the same time, human flesh, bones, and organs—shattered by a single horizontal strike—tumbled across the ground. Just like the hundreds of fanatics who had fallen before them.
hunks.sol: At the same time, flesh, bones, and organs—torn apart by a single horizontal strike—tumbled across the ground. Hundreds of fanatics had already fallen the same way.

hunks.baseline: Someone’s voice reached my ears. Of course, it belonged to one of the fanatics, someone whose face and name I didn’t know—and an enemy I had to kill.
hunks.sol: A voice reached my ears. It belonged to a fanatic whose face and name I didn’t know. An enemy I had to kill.

hunks.baseline: A familiar bell rang as Finger Qi shot from the hand I thrust out without even looking.
hunks.sol: I thrust out a hand without looking. Finger Qi shot from it, and a familiar bell rang.

hunks.baseline: Most of them probably hadn’t understood even a fraction of what had just happened before their eyes.
hunks.sol: Most of them probably couldn’t understand even a quarter of what they’d just seen.

hunks.baseline: How their comrades had died. Why they couldn’t wound me, even with so many fighters.
hunks.sol: How their comrades had died. Why so many of them still couldn’t wound me.

hunks.baseline: And those questions would remain unanswered even after they died.
hunks.sol: They would die with those questions unanswered.

hunks.baseline: Except for one man.
hunks.sol: All except one.

hunks.baseline: A straight spearhead collided with the curved blade of a saber shaped like a crescent moon.
hunks.sol: My spearhead struck the crescent curve of a saber.

hunks.baseline: The thunderous impact made my ears ring. I blocked the attack before its piercing whistle reached me, then looked at the old man beyond the white scimitar’s blade.
hunks.sol: The impact made my ears ring. I’d blocked the attack before I heard it coming. Now I stared past the white scimitar’s blade at the old man holding it.

hunks.baseline: Auras of different colors collided, sparking like lightning. A small explosion waited at their tips.
hunks.sol: Auras of different colors collided, throwing off sparks like lightning. Then came a small explosion.

hunks.baseline: The impact roared like cannon fire and traveled along my spearhead.
hunks.sol: The impact roared like cannon fire and traveled down my spear.

hunks.baseline: Unable to withstand its incredible force, I staggered backward. Seeing the old man standing firm in place, I realized something.
hunks.sol: Its force drove me backward. The old man hadn’t moved an inch, and the sight made me realize something.

hunks.baseline: A smile formed on the old man’s wrinkled lips.
hunks.sol: A smile formed on his wrinkled lips.

hunks.baseline: Two entirely different energies, never before revealed, coexisted along the scimitar’s blade, still pointed at me.
hunks.sol: Two entirely different energies, neither of which he’d revealed until now, coexisted along the scimitar’s blade pointed at me.

hunks.baseline: As those two words crossed my mind, the old man continued.
hunks.sol: As the words crossed my mind, the old man continued.

hunks.baseline: A hollow laugh escaped me before I could stop it.
hunks.sol: A hollow laugh escaped me.

hunks.baseline: The Doppelganger hadn’t raised only Michael Silbert. It had chosen its most loyal, most insane fanatic and taught him how to wield magical power.
hunks.sol: The Doppelganger hadn’t raised only Michael Silbert. It had chosen its most loyal, most insane fanatic and taught him to wield magical power.

hunks.baseline: If there had been more fanatics gifted enough to accept two opposing energies, the Doppelganger would’ve churned out half-human, half-demon monsters like they were coming off an assembly line.
hunks.sol: If more fanatics had been capable of accepting those two opposing energies, the Doppelganger would’ve churned out half-human, half-demon monsters like they were coming off an assembly line.

hunks.baseline: “I knew you were out of your mind from the start…but you’re one seriously crazy old bastard.”
hunks.sol: “I knew you were out of your mind from the start…but you’re no ordinary crazy old bastard.”

hunks.baseline: The old man shook his head and looked at me with gray eyes.
hunks.sol: The old man shook his head and fixed his gray eyes on me.

hunks.baseline: “You know nothing. Dozens, hundreds died trying to be chosen by God. But I alone survived.”
hunks.sol: “You know nothing. Dozens, hundreds died trying to be chosen by God. I alone did not.”

hunks.baseline: “So this ‘chosen by God’ thing you’re talking about just means mixing a human and a monster half and half? Then does that make a half-and-half order of black-bean noodles and spicy seafood noodles God’s warrior too?”
hunks.sol: “So being ‘chosen by God’ just means mixing a human and a monster half and half? Does that make a half-and-half order of black-bean noodles and spicy seafood noodles a warrior of God too?”

hunks.baseline: “The great Prophet said that monsters, too, are God’s creations—and calamities sent to punish the fallen humans of this world.”
hunks.sol: “The great Prophet said that monsters, too, are God’s creations—calamities sent to punish the fallen humans of this world.”

hunks.baseline: With every word, the madness in his faith showed through.
hunks.sol: The madness in his faith came through with every word.

hunks.baseline: But a madman doesn’t know he’s saying crazy things.
hunks.sol: But a madman doesn’t know he’s talking crazy.

hunks.baseline: Even if the Doppelganger gathered every fanatic in one place and offered a nationally televised apology, they wouldn’t believe it.
hunks.sol: Even if the Doppelganger gathered every fanatic in one place and made a public apology to the entire nation, they wouldn’t believe it.

hunks.baseline: Their faith was their entire lives, their reason for living, even something tied to the afterlife.
hunks.sol: Their faith was their whole life, their reason for living. It was even bound up with what they believed awaited them after death.

hunks.baseline: In the end, there was only one thing I could say to fanatics like that.
hunks.sol: In the end, there was only one thing I could say to fanatics like them.

hunks.baseline: “You fucking lunatics. It’s a waste of time talking to you.”
hunks.sol: “You fucking lunatics. Talking to you is a waste of time.”

hunks.baseline: The old man approached me. The fanatics, who had hesitated for a moment, once again burned with fighting spirit.
hunks.sol: The old man came toward me. The fanatics who had faltered found their fighting spirit again.

hunks.baseline: “Your steps will never reach the Prophet.”
hunks.sol: “You will never reach the Prophet.”

hunks.baseline: I shot forward like the wind as I answered.
hunks.sol: I shot forward like the wind.

hunks.baseline: That brief exchange had given my body a moment to recover from the strain of the fierce battle. It had also been enough to assess the situation.
hunks.sol: Our brief exchange had given my body time to recover from the strain of battle. It had also given me time to assess the situation.

hunks.baseline: The Hunters’ shouts, which had been distant, were drawing closer.
hunks.sol: The Hunters’ shouts were getting closer.

hunks.baseline: But to overcome a disadvantage of more than ten to one and win this fight, we had to cut off the head.
hunks.sol: But to overcome odds of more than ten to one and win, we had to cut off the head.

hunks.baseline: It was the best I could do before chasing the Doppelganger, which was still fleeing even now.
hunks.sol: It was the best thing I could do before chasing the Doppelganger, which was still fleeing.

hunks.baseline: My spear pierced through three fanatics and emerged on the other side.
hunks.sol: My spear drove through three fanatics and came free.

hunks.baseline: Without a trace of hesitation, the old man used his subordinates as bait and swung his scimitar at my neck.
hunks.sol: Without hesitation, the old man threw his subordinates in as bait and swung his scimitar at my neck.

hunks.baseline: I bent at the waist and dodged the slash. It cut apart the fanatics charging at me from behind.
hunks.sol: I bent at the waist. The slash missed me and cut apart the fanatics charging from behind.

hunks.baseline: The old man sprang back to prepare for my counterattack and shouted in a cold voice.
hunks.sol: The old man sprang back, ready for my counterattack, and shouted in a cold voice.

hunks.baseline: “That demon is trying to harm the great Prophet! Stop him with your lives!”
hunks.sol: “That demon means to harm the great Prophet! Give your lives to stop him!”

hunks.baseline: He might’ve been the most fanatical of the fanatics, but the experience he’d gained over the years was no joke.
hunks.sol: He might’ve been a fanatic among fanatics, but the years had taught him a thing or two.

hunks.baseline: He knew exactly what his job was, and he stayed cool-headed even in the heat of battle.
hunks.sol: He knew exactly what his job was, and he kept his head even in the heat of battle.

hunks.baseline: *If this drags on any longer…I’ll really lose him for good.*
hunks.sol: *If this drags on…I’ll lose him for good.*

hunks.baseline: I thought—or rather, calculated—as I cut down the fanatics charging from every direction like moths to a flame.
hunks.sol: As I cut down the fanatics rushing in from every direction like moths to a flame, I thought. No—I calculated.

hunks.baseline: How much strength I could bring to bear right now.
hunks.sol: How much strength I could muster right now.

hunks.baseline: How I could end this fight as quickly as possible.
hunks.sol: How to end this fight as quickly as possible.

hunks.baseline: And finally, how much strength I’d have left by the time I could chase the Doppelganger again.
hunks.sol: And how much I’d have left when I could finally chase the Doppelganger again.

hunks.baseline: Then, amid the unending blood and screams, I realized I’d been thinking about something stupid.
hunks.sol: Then, amid the blood and screams, I realized how stupid that was.

hunks.baseline: *When the hell did I start calculating every little thing like this?*
hunks.sol: *Fuck. When did I start calculating every little thing?*

hunks.baseline: When had it started? Every moment was a struggle.
hunks.sol: When had it started? Every moment had become a struggle.

hunks.baseline: Whenever that happened, I had to forget the past and erase the future from my mind.
hunks.sol: Each time, I’d had to forget the past and put the future out of my mind.

hunks.baseline: That was how you survived. Only by betting everything on the present could you think about the past and move toward the future.
hunks.sol: That was how I survived. Only by staking everything on the present could I live to look back and move forward.

hunks.baseline: A searing pain ran down my back. My exhausted body felt as heavy as a waterlogged cotton blanket. Weapons came at me like big and small gears turning in tandem, leaving wounds all over my body.
hunks.sol: Hot pain ran down my back. My exhausted body felt as heavy as waterlogged cotton. Weapons came at me like gears turning together, large and small, opening wounds all over me.

hunks.baseline: But because of that, my hesitant body and mind woke up completely.
hunks.sol: But the pain woke up every part of me that had been holding back.

hunks.baseline: I clenched my teeth against the pain and hurled the spear I held in a reverse grip at the fanatics charging straight at me.
hunks.sol: I clenched my teeth and hurled the spear I held in a reverse grip at the fanatics charging straight at me.

hunks.baseline: There was barely room to throw a spear, but one step was all I needed.
hunks.sol: The space was too tight for a proper throw, but one step was all I needed.

hunks.baseline: Flesh and blood were crushed. The pain was enough to make them forget their faith, and they screamed.
hunks.sol: Flesh and blood were crushed. They screamed with pain enough to make them forget their faith.

hunks.baseline: The old man’s command rang out among them.
hunks.sol: The old man’s command rang out through their cries.

hunks.baseline: I spat out the blood running between my lips and reached out. The Flame Divine Palm I’d been saving for a more efficient fight erupted.
hunks.sol: I spat out the blood running between my lips and reached out. The Flame Divine Palm I’d held back for the sake of an efficient fight erupted.

hunks.baseline: The fanatics crowding around me went down, engulfed in flames.
hunks.sol: The fanatics packed around me went down in flames.

hunks.baseline: I sensed them hesitate at the sight of their comrades writhing in hideous agony.
hunks.sol: At the sight of their comrades writhing in agony, the others faltered.

hunks.baseline: Blue-white flames lit up the darkness, scorching flesh and turning the blood and bones within to ash.
hunks.sol: Blue-white flames lit the darkness. They burned flesh and turned the blood and bones within it to ash.

hunks.baseline: One fanatic, who had unconsciously stepped backward before that cruel, dazzling sight of a mass execution by fire, suddenly had his head fly into the air.
hunks.sol: One of the fanatics, backing away without realizing it from the cruel, dazzling spectacle of people burning alive, lost his head.

hunks.baseline: Along with the belated sound of a blade cutting through flesh, the old man—who had vanished from sight to escape my notice—gave a chilly command.
hunks.sol: The sound of the cut came a moment later. The old man, who had slipped out of my sight, gave a cold command.

hunks.baseline: By the time I spotted the archers with dark-colored bows among the now much thinner ranks of fanatics, it was already too late.
hunks.sol: By the time I spotted the archers and their dark bows through the thinning ranks of fanatics, it was too late.

hunks.baseline: Indiscriminate fire rained down on friend and foe alike.
hunks.sol: The arrows rained down without regard for friend or foe.

hunks.baseline: The fanatics hesitating around me fell like straw, and the arrows, brimming with mana, pierced their bodies and came straight for me.
hunks.sol: The fanatics hesitating around me fell like straw. Mana-laden arrows pierced their bodies and kept coming toward me.

hunks.baseline: An unusually long whistle dragged through the air.
hunks.sol: The whistle of their flight seemed to stretch on and on.

hunks.baseline: And dark arrowheads, wrapped in blood and mana.
hunks.sol: Dark arrowheads wrapped in blood and mana.

hunks.baseline: In the moment the world slowed, a thought came to me with absolute certainty.
hunks.sol: As the world slowed, one thought came to me with absolute certainty.

hunks.baseline: Of course, I could knock aside half of them. Of the rest, I could somehow twist my body to evade half.
hunks.sol: I could knock aside half of them. Of those left, I could twist out of the way of another half somehow.

hunks.baseline: But the Fire Dragon Armor hadn’t finished repairing itself, and that didn’t change the fact that I’d have to take some damage.
hunks.sol: But the Fire Dragon Armor hadn’t finished repairing itself. I would still have to take some damage.

hunks.baseline: But why?
A strange feeling came over me.
hunks.sol: Then why did that feel wrong?

hunks.baseline: It was as if my instincts were rejecting the judgment my mind had made.
hunks.sol: My instincts seemed to reject the judgment my mind had made.

hunks.baseline: And I had a sense of déjà vu, as if my whole body’s awareness were taking another step into a realm I didn’t know existed.
hunks.sol: A strange sense of déjà vu ran through me, as though every part of me were taking another step into an unknown realm.

hunks.baseline: A strange certainty, like a conviction, took over my body and mind. An inexplicable tickling sensation began around the center of my chest and spread through my entire body.
hunks.sol: The conviction took hold of my body and mind. An inexplicable tickle began near the center of my chest and spread through me.

hunks.baseline: I reached out like a man in a trance, toward the dozens of arrows almost at my face.
hunks.sol: I reached out as if in a trance, toward the dozens of arrows almost at my face.

hunks.baseline: I stared silently at the arrows stopped in midair, then snapped my fingers.
hunks.sol: I stared at the arrows stopped in midair, then snapped my fingers.

hunks.baseline: The arrows pointed toward the enemy. And once again, the power of my newly advanced Middle Dantian pressed down on the space around us.
hunks.sol: The arrows turned toward the enemy. The qi of my Middle Dantian, advanced another step, pressed down on the space around us.

hunks.baseline: As the clear chimes pierced my ears, I smiled at the old man, frozen like a statue.
hunks.sol: As clear chimes rang in my ears, I smiled at the old man, frozen like a statue.

hunks.baseline: “Whoa. I did it?”
hunks.sol: “Whoa. It worked?”

hunks.baseline: The arrows’ powerful whistle swallowed the words he was about to say.
hunks.sol: The fierce whistle swallowed the rest of his words.
